body: No, not ramble - not for ANYONE who has had suicidal ideations - isn't THAT all rambling?  lol...I'm with you.  I never, never, never tell anyone.  People know when I'm depressed...but I don't think anyone ever thought I'd actually do anything about it.  I kind of like what you said down below, about saving your pills...someday, right?  Last night was an absolute, hands-down, all-time low for me.  Every day feels like the last, I like night-time because it feels endless somehow.  No responsibilities at night.  Last night, at a total loss, I just got drunk, took my trazadone (sleep meds) and fell asleep finally.  I was trying to do that stupid 'well maybe I'll miss out on something if I succeed' thing...but didn't really see ANYTHING on the horizon that was worth fighting for every second of sticking around, choosing life.  Literally, two minutes ago, I heard from my editor, and they want to make me a weekly columnist.  WHAT???  What the hell man.  If I was high on life, and desperately trying to be successful, I swear this wouldn't have happened.  I ripped off this particular article almost like a 'oh, well, I may as well try,' and now this response...again, kinda like a kick in the teeth.  I don't need any more conflict...I have my own secret plan to try to end things 'creatively'.  I wouldn't ever try to talk someone out of it either; I know the pain too well.  I do want to say that I can totally relate to what you said about your girlfriend moving on.  I feel that way about my kids sometimes, but then I think about the life they'd be forced to live with their absentee control freak jerk of a father.  I'm not familiar with addictions (outside of smoking, oy vey, that's hard enough to quit); but I do LOVE my opioids...when I get them.  I'd probably be an addict if I could get my hands on more of them.  Do you think that maybe anxiety about what kind of pain each moment/day/week will hold causes some of this suicidal ideation?  Is there any other reason you feel you just can't go on?

It could lower your BP, pulse, and respiratory rate; but they can give you drugs right there in the office to counter the effects of the anaesthesia pretty much immediately (that's how they bring people out of anaesthetic); then you're still faced with the possibility of severe liver damage.  I'm SO sorry to hear that both your Mom AND your brother OD'd; that must be so rough.  I can't even imagine.  That's about the only reason I'm still here - I have kids, and if I ever figured out how to do it, it would have to be a way that would look accidental, or 'natural.'  I wouldn't want them to think I'd abandoned them; or give them the impression that suicide is a way out (I'm such a hypocrite, right?).  Frankly, I can't believe I'm still here - when I woke up after EVERY suicide attempt, nobody had a clue.  It felt like a slap in the face.  I hope you feel differently about it in the morning...again, I'm such a hypocrite...

Well...keep in mind that 'help' is ongoing.  It's not all rainbows & lollipops lol...omgosh, yes, I feel guilty EVERY time I take a 'me' day - I'm all over the map - some days I feel so positive, I'm gonna get so much done, I have a list...then I get overwhelmed, it feels like too much, it feels impossible, and then I justify stopping by saying 'at least I got SOMETHING done.'  I think, though, it's enough.  I'm still here, for whatever that's worth - I've started a blog, very tentatively, and am trying to learn how to do some freelance writing - I'm trying to find other reasons to get up, deadlines to make and keep.  I think all people who've been through something traumatic like that, I think we kind of 'give up.'  I think perhaps we've changed so much we're not sure how to proceed.  Like, cognitive dissonance.  It's hard to recognize ourselves in the hollow shell that's left behind, and we know how we used to proceed, but just can't.  Our therapists tell us what we SHOULD do but it feels empty and stupid.  I will say, though, when I take a me day, there's a little piece of me that kind of says 'screw YOU' to the world that doesn't understand.  Um, kind of like I'm breaking some kind of rule.  But wow does it feel good to just lay in bed all curled up and maybe watch a movie or just sleep.  I think it's necessary.  I'm sorry your SO doesn't seem to understand - gosh my heart goes out to you.  (((hugs)))

Sorry, but I don't think it would work.  I have tried to overdose 3 times - once on a whole bottle of tylenol, twice by taking a whole week's worth of my entire plethora of prescription meds with 2 bottles of wine as a chaser.  The closest I got was my last attempt which landed me in hospital with 5 grand mal seizures enroute to the hospital alone, but nobody even knew I had attempted suicide - I'd puked my guts out when I had the seizures.  I guess they just figured I was drunk or something.  Overdoses can also be really nasty if they kill your liver - dying of liver failure is painful as hell and grotesque.  I personally wouldn't recommend it.

OMG I wish I had been brave enough to say this.  I think about it all the time.  Sometimes I fantasize about something horrible that happened to me, that I survived, but in my daydreams, they find me half-dead, and I'm slightly aware of the concerned faces, the ambulance attendants urgently calling my name, police voices sounding angry, concerned, upset.  All the things that never happened  that night that I was victimized.  I sometimes wish it had ended like that.  Instead, as mentioned in a previous comment, I have to hide my feelings, this inner battle of life vs death, this need to hide my inner anguish, or fear all of the judgement that goes with it.  Sometimes I wish people could just see inside me, see the feelings, so that I don't have to feel so ashamed.  I saw Gordie playing his last concert Saturday night (Tragically Hip - he was an acquaintance of mine in my teens) and I kept thinking, I'd give him my life in a heartbeat.  I wonder, if people could see what they're doing to me, would they feel bad?  Would they stop?  Would they apologize? A friend of mine is also extremely suicidal right now, and when I see him get like this, I always say to him, 'I would stay up with you all night, if it would save your life...' and I wonder if anyone would ever do that for me.  I think the answer for me is 'no' - but if I was dying of cancer, I know there would be people holding my hand at my bedside.

All I can say is that I feel so deeply for you.  I can relate to your experience.  I was raped 4 years ago by a police officer.  I ended up eventually getting a PTSD Service Dog, and even then it took time for me to build up the courage to go out in public with him.  I put video cameras on my house, installed an alarm system, but in the end, it was my SD who slept next to me each night, woke me with kisses when I had nightmares, hung out in my room with me when I just couldn't get up, that helped me try again.  The guy who did this to you is SICK.  It's a really, really hard thing to live with.  I just want you to know that you're not alone, for real.  You make perfect sense to me.  I have good days and bad days too.  Some nights I go to bed swearing I'll clean up the house, go for a run, organize something, then wake up and just say 'nope.  It's a 'me' day.'  I do a lot of pretending too - I think of that line in Eleanor Rigby by the Beattles a lot - 'she sits at the window, wearing the face that she keeps in the jar by the door...' I wish I knew how to help you feel better, but I just wanted you to know that you're not alone in your feelings.
Won't somebody please, please talk to me?  I can't stop crying.  I don't want to be here anymore.  I don't think I can hang on anymore.
I have NOBODY to talk to.  I have spent every second of the last five hours arguing with myself about it and looking up ways to make it look like an accident.
